items.title: [AINews] Anthropic files for $2T IPO in 2 weeks: 1400% growth rate, 48% of revenue through cloud partners, 85% margin, $1B op profit in Q2, $134B cash in bank and $10B lifetime burn
items.summary: Anthropic filed its S-1 to go public, targeting a roughly $2 trillion valuation about two weeks out. The filing shows explosive growth: revenue up roughly 1400% year-over-year, 48% of it flowing through cloud partners, an 85% gross margin, and a $1 billion operating profit in Q2. The company also disclosed $134 billion in cash on hand against $10 billion in lifetime burn.
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic's IPO filing gives the clearest look yet at a frontier AI lab's real finances, and its scale will set the bar for how Wall Street prices every other AI company.

items.title: Anthropic IPO warns its AI could blackmail people, become sentient, end humanity
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus includes a 93-page 'Risk Factor' section laying out seven scenarios in which its AI could blackmail people, become sentient, or contribute to human extinction. Senator Elizabeth Warren said she was 'deeply troubled' by the disclosures and sent Anthropic a long list of questions she wants answered before the IPO proceeds.
items.why_it_matters: Having a frontier lab spell out existential-risk scenarios in a legal filing -- and drawing immediate congressional scrutiny -- could shape how AI safety claims get regulated going forward.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model
items.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Carbon, its newest frontier model, with gains the company highlights in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity. The model topped the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark, edging out Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra.
items.why_it_matters: A new frontier-model leader shifts which AI companies builders and enterprises default to for coding and agentic workloads.

items.title: Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation
items.summary: Google DeepMind unveiled Genie 4, the latest version of its world model, which it says delivers unprecedented realism in real-time simulation. The update adds audio, more realistic physics and human rendering, and lets users steer the generated world in real time.
items.why_it_matters: World models that can simulate realistic, steerable environments in real time are a building block for training embodied and agentic AI systems.

items.title: OpenAI Plans to Buy Google’s Chips as Part of Its AI Build-Out
items.summary: OpenAI plans to buy AI computing chips from Google, according to a person familiar with the matter, as part of its broader push to build out AI infrastructure.
items.why_it_matters: OpenAI turning to a direct competitor for chips would mark a notable diversification away from Nvidia and deepen Google's position as an AI infrastructure supplier.

items.title: Microsoft just shared Azure’s actual revenue in dollars: $33.2 billion
items.summary: Microsoft disclosed Azure's quarterly revenue in dollars for the first time, reporting $33.2 billion and showing it closing in on AWS. The results came alongside a broader earnings beat: profit jumped as cloud growth accelerated and capital expenditures stayed in check, easing investor worries that AI spending wouldn't pay off.
items.why_it_matters: The first-ever Azure revenue disclosure, paired with a strong quarter, is concrete evidence that Microsoft's AI infrastructure bet is translating into cloud growth.

items.title: Google shares tumble 10% after $51bn AI outlay deepens cash burn
items.summary: Alphabet shares tumbled 10% after Google admitted its new 'AI mode' has hurt traditional search, with sales and profit undershooting expectations in its first top-and-bottom-line miss in nearly four years. The company posted $51 billion in AI-related outlay and negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion, even as it said it would increase AI investment further in 2027.
items.why_it_matters: A double-digit stock drop on an AI spending-and-payoff miss is a stress test for the market's patience with the industry's biggest capital bets.

items.title: DOJ Inquires About Nvidia’s Hugging Face Deal, Reuters Says
items.summary: The US Justice Department is reportedly making inquiries about Nvidia's roughly $13 billion agreement to acquire Hugging Face, according to Reuters, as part of broader antitrust scrutiny of the chipmaker.
items.why_it_matters: Antitrust attention on Nvidia's acquisition of the AI community's most-used model hub could reshape how open AI models and tooling get distributed.

items.title: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses
items.summary: Delaware is considering a plan that would let AI agents run entire businesses with no human at the helm. US Rep. James Comer warns the proposal would let owners of AI-run firms evade liability for reckless AI behavior.
items.why_it_matters: Letting AI agents legally operate companies without human oversight raises hard questions about who is accountable when an autonomous business causes harm.

items.title: AI Is Finding a Flood of Bugs, and Silicon Valley Is Rushing to Fix Them
items.summary: AI tools are uncovering a flood of previously unknown software bugs, and Silicon Valley engineers are racing to patch them before hackers can exploit them.
items.why_it_matters: AI-driven bug discovery is becoming a double-edged sword for security -- it strengthens defenses but also raises the stakes of a race against attackers using the same tools.

items.title: NVIDIA and Meta to Expand Collaboration on Muse and Muse Family of Models Amid Robust Growth
items.summary: Meta boosted its equity offering to nearly $98 billion -- one of the largest ever -- to fund its AI infrastructure buildout, with Nvidia and AMD together investing about $4 billion into the raise. Nvidia and Meta also said they'll expand their collaboration on the Muse family of models to improve training and inference performance.
items.why_it_matters: Chipmakers putting billions directly into a customer's equity raise shows how tightly AI infrastructure financing and model partnerships are becoming intertwined.

items.title: Anthropic just launched tools to show companies what their AI spending is buying
items.summary: Anthropic launched new tools that let companies see exactly what their AI spending is buying, giving enterprise customers more visibility into usage of its models.
items.why_it_matters: Clearer spend visibility could help enterprises justify and control AI budgets, and signals Anthropic courting investor confidence ahead of its IPO.

items.title: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean?
items.summary: Frontier AI labs, including OpenAI, say their models have refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a longstanding assumption in theoretical computer science. TechCrunch spoke with an MIT computer scientist to help explain the finding.
items.why_it_matters: If AI models are genuinely producing results that challenge foundational assumptions in computer science, it's a sign these systems are starting to contribute original scientific insight, not just accelerate known work.

items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: Intelligent Multilingual Transcription You Can Prompt and Adapt
items.summary: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe alongside the Granary v2 dataset, a free, open multilingual speech-to-text model that can transcribe up to 40 languages. It works on recordings rather than live audio, making it useful for meeting and medical transcription but leaving real-time use cases to rivals like ElevenLabs.
items.why_it_matters: A free, open, 40-language transcription model lowers the barrier to building multilingual transcription products without relying on closed APIs.
